## Context / Problem
Long-running MCP and review-bot processes mix startup deployment policy with per-operation config and ambient auth reads. Static Gerrit/GitHub/LLM/telemetry material can change underneath an in-progress operation or be reread inconsistently. RP-04 requires restart/redeploy rotation for static bindings while preserving request-scoped inbound auth and SDK-native refresh.

## Outcome
Compose non-secret startup policy and live runtime bindings once when MCP/review-bot services start; create a fresh non-secret `OperationSnapshot` for each operation/request. Review-bot Gerrit/GitHub/LLM capabilities are typed and adapter-local. Inbound MCP bearer tokens remain transient request context, never config. Optional Langfuse/OTLP setup remains fail-open/no-op and cannot change the underlying operation result.

## Plan
1. Update MCP construction so deployment/startup config is captured once, each tool call composes its own S1 operation snapshot, and existing OAuth/JWKS/introspection/proxy verification stays request-scoped under ADR 0050.
2. Update review-bot config/app/Gerrit client to compose static provider bindings at startup, validate decision-bearing auth before accepting a job/webhook, and pass S4 `LLMRuntime` plus focused Git/Gerrit policy into each operation. Do not expose stronger server identity through CLI/MCP inputs.
3. Bind Langfuse/OTLP once at startup using provider-specific static input. Missing/partial/rejected telemetry disables telemetry with a redacted diagnostic and no operation-result change; security/load-bearing auth remains fail-closed.
4. Document and test rotation: changing static env/file material does not rebind a running process; a restarted process observes it; revoked old auth fails without principal fallback; official refreshable capabilities may refresh in process.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- Service/component tests run two operations around environment/file mutation and assert static runtime identity is unchanged while operation-scoped non-secret config is freshly composed where intended.
- MCP auth interface suites prove inbound tokens die with the request and never enter startup/operation snapshots, logs, caches, schemas, or subprocess environments.
- Review-bot verified-fake tests cover valid/missing/conflicting/revoked Gerrit/GitHub auth, webhook acceptance, one selected integration, LLM runtime forwarding, and no fallback principal.
- Observability tests use partial/rejected credentials and exporter failure; the exact operation result remains equal and only telemetry is disabled.
- [operator-attested] AWS review-bot deploy/E2E canary records change/run ids, startup binding kinds, vote/result, retry counts, timestamp, and redacted diagnostics.

## Compatibility / rollback
During expansion, service constructors accept optional runtime bindings and may use the legacy startup composition facade. Rollback before cutover selects that facade and restarts/redeploys. MCP wire/tool schemas, webhook auth protocol, Gerrit vote schema, and LLM result schemas remain unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] MCP and review-bot tests prove startup bindings stay stable across ambient mutation while each new operation receives the intended fresh non-secret snapshot.
- [x] MCP inbound bearer/OAuth material remains request-local and absent from startup/operation snapshots, serialization, logs, caches, child environments, and tool schemas.
- [x] Review-bot decision-bearing auth is validated before job/provider work, only the selected integration is constructed, and revoked/missing/conflicting auth never falls back to another principal.
- [x] Static binding replacement is observed only after process restart/redeploy; native refreshable capability behavior remains SDK-owned.
- [x] Partial/rejected Langfuse/OTLP auth disables telemetry without changing the underlying operation result, while security/load-bearing auth remains fail-closed.
- [x] [operator-attested] The AWS review-bot deploy/E2E canary passes and records the required redacted provenance.
  provenance: environment=AWS-hosted rebar review bot + GitHub Actions CI; principal=review-bot production principal (deployed) + CI reconciler; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Gerrit 1861 PS4 (147caa1ebe): the AWS-hosted rebar review bot processed this change end-to-end (event->clone->review->signed vote) and cast LLM-Review +1, and CI cast Verified +1 running the S5 held-out oracle over the NEW startup-binding/decision-auth/runtime-forwarding code; startup binding kinds = all-None ambient LLMRuntime (SDK-owned creds) + non-secret Gerrit/GitHub/LLM ReceiverConfig policy; vote/result = LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1 / PASS; retries = 0; redacted diagnostics = none; no token/credential material recorded; full evidence in the operator-attestation comment on this ticket.
